name: tacli-promo
_stage: The tile is the WINDOW, and the game fills the window's CLIENT rect — so it
is the client that has to be 4:3, not the tile. The title bar takes 5.5% of
the height, so a 1024x768 tile leaves a 1022x724 client (1.412) and every
frame of footage was stretched 5.9% wide. 1024x813 leaves 1022x767 (1.3325).
The 64px gap is the desktop showing between windows — it is what makes the
wide shot read as 'a desktop full of games' rather than one big texture.
_camera: cols = how many window columns fit across the frame, interpolated in log
space. Centre (512,384) is hero 1's middle; (1056,800) the 2x2 block's.
The camera is FROZEN whenever text is on screen: 0-7.5s for hero 1, and
10.5-25.0s across terminals 2-4. Both holds must be EXACTLY constant in
`cols` — a drift of 3.05 to 2.95 looks like a hold in the file and is a slow
zoom in the picture, creeping the tiles 593.8 -> 599.3 px and making every
glyph crawl. Measured on the prompt region, temporal 2nd difference:
any push 7.453, frozen 0.000. There is no such thing as a subtle push here.
cols 1.476 on the opening is ARITHMETIC, not taste: the hero window has to
sit inside the frame with 5% of the height clear above and below it.
visible world height = cols * pitch_x * (out_h / out_w) = cols * 612
At the 1.3 this opened on, the visible height was 795.6 against an 813-tall
tile, so the window was 17 units TALLER than the frame and its top and
bottom borders were cut off -- it read as a window with no edges. 1.476
leaves 45 units of desktop top and bottom. It also matches the 2x2 block at
cols 3.05, which sits at 1690/(3.05*612) = 90.5% of the height: beats 1 and
2 are now framed the same way instead of one bleeding and one not. The
16:9 ratio is what makes the sides wider (18.1% each) -- a 1.26:1 window
cannot be inset vertically and tight horizontally at the same time.
_windows: The four hero windows. Each opens as a terminal, types its command, prints
output, then cross-fades into the game in the SAME rect — that is beat 2.
`clip` is the clip id used by --backend clip; `variant` only colours the
Window 0's `output` is the REAL transcript, captured 2026-09-10 from the
shoot. Windows 1-3 are still the placeholder format and get replaced when

_fill: The grid behind the heroes. Each cell gets a random clip and a random time
offset so no two tiles are in step. Range covers the cols=44 wide shot with
reveal.not_before is the hard gate that keeps beats 1-4 honest: until 22.0s
the desktop holds exactly the scripted windows (one, then four), so no
neighbour creeps into frame. At 22.0 the first ring fades up over `wave`
seconds — the desktop filling is a deliberate shot. Every outer ring is
already open `lead` seconds before the camera reaches it, so nothing pops
on screen. The times come from the camera path, so retiming the pull-back
retimes the reveal with no hand-edited open times.
_captions: The Card treatment: full-frame typographic cards, chosen from the five
prototype cuts on 2026-09-10. Claims are checked in the ta-video-montage
skill's table. Captions wrap and shrink to fit, so a long line is safe.
Beat 1's card sits AFTER the terminal flips to the game (4.6s, not 1.2s):
over the terminal it covered the command and the lines it printed.

captions.sub: no menu, no map setup, no clicking
edit it, commit it, re-run it
or as many as the machine will hold

captions.text: Control units, spawn more on demand, send any command to a scenario as it runs.

_audio: The soundtrack, laid over the finished cut by `--audio <file>`. The PATH is
not here on purpose: it would name someone's home directory, and the track is
licensed for use inside a work rather than for redistribution, so the file
never enters this repository. promo/MUSIC.md carries the full metadata and the
dispute answer if the video is ever content-matched.
ALIGN THE MUSIC'S HIT TO THE FILM'S HIT, NOT THE FILE'S ENDS. The mp3 is
40.18s long but about 5s of that is digital silence: the music peaks at 31.5s
and its tail resolves by ~35s, which is why the source lists it as 0:36.
Aligning 57.0 - 40.18 = 16.82 put the peak at 48s and left the climax -- the
1600-window wide shot and the title card -- playing over dead air.
start 20.0 lands the peak at 51.5s, exactly where the title card appears on
the full wall, and the tail resolves at ~55s under it. The ~20s of silence
before it is forced arithmetic, not taste: 35s of music cannot cover 57s of
film AND finish at the end. It falls over the opening, where one terminal
types one command, and that plays better dry anyway.
